info.description: Pirate ships race around a ring of islands digging up buried treasure. Every island you stop at hands you treasure, forces treasure on you or lets you rob the captain moored there, while a wandering storm blows ships and cargo across the sea and a hold of more than seven treasure capsizes. The first captain to land ten treasure in their own harbour wins.
info.ruleText:
Several pirate ships cruise a ring of 28 lonely islands looking for buried treasure. Dig it up, load it on board and be the first to bring ten pieces safely into your own harbour - while a wandering storm, greedy rivals and your own overloaded hold do their best to stop you.

On your turn you roll one die. A number sails your ship that many islands onward, following the arrows; an island has room for two ships, a third one sails on to the next free island. Islands with an open chest let you take as much of the treasure as you like, up to three; a closed red chest blinds you with greed and forces two on board; on an island without a chest the arriving captain may take up to two treasure from the ship moored there, or push up to two onto it. A hold takes seven treasure at most - one too many and the ship capsizes and the whole cargo sinks.

Each colour has a harbour beside its own entrance island. Only its owner may turn in, and the rest of the move is lost when they do; the treasure is unloaded there and the ship sets out again on the next turn.

The storm face of the die lets you sail one single island and then drift the storm against the sailing direction - up to five islands with two players, four with three, three with four. If the storm comes to rest on an island with ships, the wind wheel decides their fate: blown one island on, one treasure to every other captain, swept safely home, or two treasure washed into the sea.
info.helpText:
Goal

Be the first captain to land 10 treasure in your own harbour. The number on your harbour plate - and the anchor counter next to your seat - is what you have landed so far.

Setup

Everybody clicks a seat, then somebody presses the anchor button on the right. All ships return to their harbours, the storm is placed on a random island and a random captain starts.

Your turn

Press the big dice button on the right (or click the die itself). Everything that follows is worked out for you; you only answer the questions.
  • A number - your ship sails that many islands clockwise, following the dark arrows. If your own harbour entrance is on the way you are asked whether you want to sail in, unload and start a new voyage; the rest of the move is then lost.
  • The storm symbol - you may first sail on one single island, then you drift the storm against the sailing direction (the white wind arrows): up to 5 islands with 2 players, 4 with 3 players, 3 with 4 players (0 = leave it where it is).

The 28 spaces

  • Open chest, green 3 - load as much treasure as you like, 0 to 3. The dialog suggests the largest amount your hold can take.
  • Closed chest, red 2 - greed wins: you must load 2 treasure.
  • Island without a chest - if a rival ship is moored here you may steal up to 2 treasure from it, or push up to 2 of yours onto it to make it capsize. Choose 0 to do nothing.
  • Harbour entrance - the anchor island in each corner. The harbour itself lies beside it and only its owner may sail in.
  • An island has room for two ships; a third one sails on to the next island with a free berth.
  • A ship carries at most 7 treasure. Load more and it capsizes: the whole cargo sinks and it sails on with an empty hold.

When the storm comes to rest on ships

The wind wheel in the middle of the sea is spun and shows what happens to every ship on that island:
  • Wind - the ships are blown one island onward and work that island as usual.
  • Three figures - each hit ship hands one treasure to every other captain, who has to take it aboard - a full hold capsizes. A captain lying in their harbour puts it straight into the harbour.
  • Anchor - lucky! The hit ships reach their own harbour and unload at once.
  • Splash - two treasure per hit ship wash into the sea.

Playing by hand

Nothing is ever blocked. Ships and the storm can simply be dragged from island to island, and the two counters next to your seat can be clicked to correct the cargo on board (⛵) and the treasure in your harbour (⚓) - useful for house rules, for taking a move back or for setting up a position. The dice button is only the comfortable way to play.

Shorter game

Agree on fewer than 10 treasure before you start and simply stop when somebody reaches that number - the anchor counter next to each seat shows the score.
